settings.auth.policyDescription: Authentication applies whether the panel is on loopback or exposed to the network.
settings.auth.requirePasswordHint: Every request needs a signed-in session.
settings.auth.sessionLifetimeHint: Idle timeout: 604800000 is one week of no activity. Each request restarts it.
settings.auth.trustProxyHint: Trust x-forwarded-* for the client address and protocol. 'From this machine only' is the safe choice for a proxy on the same host. 'From any caller' believes the caller's own header, so login lockout counts per forged address and can be bypassed.
settings.auth.apiTokenNote: Scripts can call the API with {code} instead of signing in.
settings.auth.noTokenNote: For shell scripts and agents, generate one with {command}.
settings.auth.defaultPasswordTitle: The default password is still in use
settings.auth.defaultPasswordText: Set your own password below. Binding beyond {address} stays refused until you do.
settings.auth.noPasswordTitle: Authentication is on but no password is set
settings.auth.noPasswordText: Nothing is actually required yet, and binding beyond {address} stays refused until a password exists.
settings.auth.exposedText: Keep the password strong, or put a TLS-terminating proxy in front of the panel.
settings.auth.passwordDescription: Stored as a scrypt hash in the secrets file, never in the config.
settings.auth.passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
settings.auth.clearPasswordHint: Authentication is switched off with it, and anyone reaching the panel is let straight in.
settings.auth.shortPasswordText: It is allowed, but longer is the only thing standing between the network and this panel.
settings.auth.passwordUpdated: Password updated. Other sessions were signed out.
settings.backup.createDescription: Pick what this archive captures. Nothing is written until you create it.
settings.backup.partialCapture: Only the chosen items are captured.
settings.backup.withoutGlobalSettings: Without the global settings, a restore can only place a workspace where the target panel already declares it.
settings.backup.passwordHint: Encrypts the archive; restoring it asks for the same password.
settings.backup.subDescription: A workspace can be captured whole or only its settings, servers, secrets and declared data paths.
settings.backup.nothingSelectable: This workspace declares nothing selectable yet.
settings.backup.leafSettingsHint: Server defaults, log retention and notifications
settings.backup.leafSecretsHint: Telegram bot token and DDNS credentials
settings.backup.entrySettingsHint: Listener, auth, host vitals and the backups policy
settings.backup.entrySecretsHint: Password hash and API token hash
settings.backup.entryWorkspaceHint: Its settings, servers, secrets and declared data paths
settings.backups.policyDescription: How many archives the panel keeps, and the extra paths every one of them captures.
settings.backups.allowHint: Off stops new archives; whatever is already on disk stays downloadable and restorable.
settings.backups.offText: Nothing new is archived until this is back on. The archives below can still be downloaded, restored and deleted.
settings.backups.keepHint: Older archives are pruned after each backup.
settings.backups.extraPathsHint: Comma separated, captured in every archive on top of what each workspace declares.
settings.backups.changeDirectory: Changing it is a file-level decision: edit {path}.
settings.backups.capturesDescription: Pick these in the create dialog. A workspace can be taken whole or only its settings, servers, secrets and declared data paths.
settings.backups.workspacesNote: This panel serves {count} workspaces; each is its own selectable entry.
settings.backups.archivesDescription: Stored in the backup directory and downloadable at any time.
settings.backups.noArchivesEnabled: Create one now to capture the panel and whichever workspaces you pick.
settings.backups.noArchivesDisabled: Nothing has been archived yet, and backups are off.
settings.ddns.loadErrorTitle: Dynamic DNS settings could not be loaded
settings.ddns.title: Dynamic DNS
settings.ddns.description: Keep these hostnames pointed at this machine's public address. Credentials live in the secrets file, never in servers.config.json.
settings.ddns.enabledHint: A pass runs on the interval below; a provider is only called when the address actually changed.
settings.ddns.intervalHint: 60000 is one minute; the default is five.
settings.ddns.ttlHint: 1 means automatic where the provider supports it.
settings.ddns.accountsDescription: One entry per API token. Credentials are stored on the server and never come back.
settings.ddns.removeAccountBlocked: Remove the hostnames using this account first
settings.ddns.noAccounts: No accounts yet. Pick a provider and add one.
settings.ddns.accountIdHint: The account id names the account and keys its stored credentials; lowercase letters, digits, `-` and `_`.
settings.ddns.hostnamesDescription: The whole list to keep updated — suba.domain.com, domain.xyz and so on.
settings.ddns.aaaaUnsupported: This provider cannot manage AAAA records.
settings.ddns.proxiedHint: Cloudflare serves this record through its own network.
settings.ddns.registeredDomainHint: Only when the provider has to be told the apex, e.g. three-label domains.
settings.ddns.credentialsDescription: Saved fields are never sent back. Saving replaces every field for this account and runs a pass right away.
settings.ddns.forgetHint: They are removed from disk and cannot be read back; you would need to paste them again.
settings.defaults.title: Server defaults
settings.defaults.description: Applied to every entry that does not set its own value.
settings.defaults.conflictFollow: Follow a detached restart of itself
settings.defaults.conflictReclaim: Replace a detached restart with a supervised copy
settings.host.title: Thresholds
settings.host.description: A threshold of 0 disables that alert. Breaches notify once, and once more on recovery.
settings.host.enabledHint: Load, memory, swap, disk and CPU temperature, on the interval below.
settings.host.intervalHint: How often the host is sampled and alerts are checked.
settings.host.diskPathsHint: Comma separated; templates like {home} are expanded.
settings.host.loadPerCpuHint: 1-minute load average divided by the core count.
settings.host.tempCelsiusHint: Linux only; ignored where the OS does not expose it.
settings.interface.title: Interface
settings.interface.description: The panel is a static site: keep the stock one, or serve your own build from the state directory.
settings.interface.panelVersionHint: The release this panel process is running — {command} prints the same number.
settings.interface.panelNameHint: Shown in the sidebar by the stock UI. A custom UI may show its own name instead.
settings.interface.uploadLabel: Upload a UI build (.zip with an index.html)
settings.interface.docsHint: See {docs} for the API contract. If a custom UI breaks the panel, {command} puts the stock one back from the terminal.
settings.interface.installed: UI replaced with {name} — refresh the page
settings.interface.restored: stock UI restored — refresh the page
settings.listener.title: Listener
settings.listener.description: Where the panel answers. Moving this restarts the panel and sends this page to the new address.
settings.listener.bindCustomHint: A specific interface address you type in below.
settings.listener.ipv4Error: Enter an IPv4 address, for example 192.168.1.20.
settings.listener.ipv4Hint: Binding beyond 127.0.0.1 needs a real password.
settings.listener.openBrowser: Open a browser when the panel comes up
settings.listener.liveAddressHint: What the listener is bound to right now; saved changes take effect after the panel rebinds.
settings.logs.title: Retention
settings.logs.description: The live view always comes from memory; these files survive a restart and feed the Logs page.
settings.logs.persistHint: Turn off to hold everything in memory only.
settings.logs.browseHint: Browse and download these files on the {logs} page.
settings.telegram.title: Telegram
settings.telegram.description: Policy lives in the config; the bot token is a secret and never comes back from the server.
settings.telegram.enabledHint: One message per event, throttled by the cooldown below.
settings.telegram.chatIdHint: Use Detect chats to fill this from the bot's updates.
settings.telegram.cooldownHint: Per server and reason, so a flapping server cannot spam.
settings.telegram.onHostHint: Disk, memory, swap, load and CPU temperature, per the thresholds under Host vitals.
settings.telegram.onDdnsHint: One message per pass that changed a record, and one for a pass that failed.
settings.telegram.tokenNote: From @BotFather — a secret, never in servers.config.json.
settings.telegram.tokenSavedPlaceholder: Saved — type a new token to replace it
settings.telegram.removeTokenHint: Notifications stop until you paste a token again.
settings.telegram.noChats: No chats found. Send /start to the bot first, then detect again.
settings.tls.title: HTTPS
settings.tls.description: Upload a PEM pair and the panel serves TLS on its own listener. A self-signed certificate is fine on a home network.
settings.tls.serveHint: Saved with Save settings; the panel rebinds and this page follows it.
settings.tls.certificateDescription: PEM-encoded certificate and its private key. Both stay in the secrets file.
settings.tls.unusableTitle: The stored certificate cannot be used
settings.tls.subject: Subject
settings.tls.noCertificateText: Upload a PEM certificate and key below, then save. HTTPS is not served until a certificate is present.
settings.tls.removeHint: TLS stays on but has nothing to serve, so the panel falls back to http once the listener rebinds.
settings.paths.dataRootHint: HHOSTED_HOME — global settings, workspaces, TLS, backups and the UI.
settings.paths.globalSettingsHint: settings.json — listener, auth, TLS policy, host vitals, backups.
settings.paths.panelAddressHint: Where this control panel is live right now.
settings.paths.workspaceSettingsHint: Server defaults, log retention, notifications, DDNS.
settings.paths.whereThingsLiveDescriptio: Read-only. Copy a path straight into a shell or an editor.
settings.paths.workspaceFilesDescription: Each workspace owns its config, settings and log directory; nothing is shared between them.
settings.restore.title: Restore a backup
settings.restore.description: Nothing is written until the plan is applied.
settings.restore.archiveHint: A stored archive, or a .zip from this machine.
settings.restore.choosePrompt: Choose what to restore — {selected} of {total} selected.
settings.restore.restartNote: The panel's own settings differ, so restart the panel afterwards.
settings.restore.reloadedNote: Restored workspaces are reloaded immediately; entries marked autostart start on their own.
settings.restore.noteReloaded: the restored servers are live, autostart entries starting
settings.restore.noteRestart: restart the panel to apply its own settings
settings.rebind.failed: The control panel did not answer on {target}. Check the console for the new listener.
